sections.sectionText: FSHN 120 (Honors section): Contemporary Nutrition. Explore the impact of food on health and wellness with an emphasis on critical thinking, reflective learning, and experiential engagement. Students will examine nutrition concepts in depth, connect course material to real-world issues such as food insecurity and health disparities, and collaborate on applied projects designed to strengthen academic and professional skills. As an Honors section, the course emphasizes discussion, active learning, and leadership in both classroom and community contexts. ***If you’re a James Scholar or honors student who wants to complete an honors project in FSHN 120, you may enroll in the online section (CRN 57561). The instructor will provide additional opportunities to complete an approved honors project there. Questions? Email burkhalt@illinois.edu.

sections.sectionText: FSHN 398: Performance Nutrition Experience with Illini Fuel! This hands-on course offers a unique opportunity to work directly with Illini Athletics and the Performance Nutrition program at the University of Illinois. Students will gain valuable, real-world experience in performance nutrition, assisting with the preparation, delivery, and management of athlete-focused nutritional support within the fueling station. To enroll, students must successfully complete an interview process and pass a background check conducted by the Department of Intercollegiate Athletics before the first week of class. You must reach out to Chloe Morrell (Chloem@illinois.edu) and Brooke Hawkins (bh17@illinois.edu) with your resume to start the interview process. Students will commit to approximately 6 hours per week (totaling 100 hours over the semester), with shifts that may include early mornings and late evenings. Attendance and participation are essential. Each shift is 2-hours minimum, counting for 2% of the final grade. To earn credit, arriving on time and staying the duration of the shift earns 1% of the grade and the other 1% is earned through arrival in the proper apparel, maintaining a positive attitude, and remaining on task (off phone) during the entirety of the shift. This course is ideal for students passionate about sports nutrition and looking to gain hands-on experience in a dynamic, fast-paced environment supporting athletic performance and recovery.

sections.sectionText: This will be a project-based course with a flexible schedule. You will work directly with the instructor to determine the schedule. The course involves learning advanced topics such as differential analysis in discrimination tests, Thurstonian modeling, multivariate techniques, clustering, and biometrics, with students managing a research project related to these areas. Weekly meetings with the instructor will guide progress, but students should expect to dedicate at least five additional hours per week to complete the assignments and learning goals. The flexible schedule allows students to work closely with the instructor. The final assessment will be a literature review or research paper based on their findings. This course emphasizes self-directed learning, critical thinking, and hands-on experience in sensory science research.

sections.sectionText: Advanced study of the behavior of water and solids in food materials, specifically in relation to food quality, ingredient functionality, stability, and safety. Major topics discussed include structure, properties, and chemistry of water and solids, water-solid interactions, and moisture management strategies, including water activity, water mobility, and solids mobility (e.g., the glass transition). Practical techniques to measure water and solid content and dynamics, including direct and indirect moisture content measurement methods, water activity, sorption isotherms, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and imaging, and differential scanning calorimetry, will also be discuss.

sections.sectionText: TITLE: Concepts in Nutritional Physiology II *** This is a two part class. You will be expected to take Concepts in Nutritional Physiology I in Fall term for 1 credit hour and Concepts in Nutritional Physiology II in Spring term for 2 credit hours.*** Concepts in Nutritional Physiology II will cover the following topics: Anatomy and physiology of the respiratory, nervous, endocrine, immune, reproductive, and urinary system. The class will have a special focus on the absorption, distribution, storage, and mobilization of macronutrients and micronutrients; The student will learn the necessary concepts on cell biology and biochemistry required to understand human physiology; The manifestation of disease as a result of nutritional imbalances in body systems; Evaluation of the effectiveness and potential toxicity of nutritional supplements commonly used in the US; Pharmacological interventions and current therapeutics against diseases related to nutritional disorders. IMPORTANT: Concepts in Nutritional Physiology II is the second part of a sequence. If you did not take Concepts in Nutritional Physiology I, please contact the instructor for approval to register.

sections.sectionText: Sports Nutrition for Dietitians: This asynchronous online course will focus on applied performance nutrition. It will provide an in-depth look at the essential role of nutrition for athletic performance, recovery and overall health. Students will learn practical applications and current performance nutrition strategies. ***Prereq: FSHN 420 or consent of instructor. Students should have a fundamental understanding of performance nutrition.***
